title: #4471 · Parser fixed; booking-v3 hint will not be fixed · support kb
text:
support desk · kb
#4471 · Parser fixed; booking-v3 hint will not be fixed

owner md-400
closed
reviewed 2026-11-13 · 0 days ago

Latest engineering disposition

The support desk’s engineering update closes the original incident on 5 October 2026. It does not say that both problems were fixed.

Engineering closed #4471 on 2026-10-05, with a different outcome per cause.

cause	unique reports	outcome	engineering evidence	GitHub closure
parser	379	FIXED	fix(dates): parse dd/mm for eu locales	issue 1 — completed
hint	33	WON'T FIX	booking-v3 form retired	issue 2 — not planned

Counts are still computed from unique report IDs and tenant-aware causes in the original export. Closing a ticket does not remove its historical reports or combine the two causes.

The hint problem is won't fix, not fixed: booking-v3 was retired. The parser was fixed. Do not copy the parser's completed status onto the hint ticket or claim the old date hint was corrected.
What changed since the initial split

Our first submission established two real causes, with one GitHub ticket per cause. The engineering update then supplied the outcome for each one:

Parser: fix(dates): parse dd/mm for eu locales. Close issue 1 as completed, citing engineering’s fixed status.
Hint: booking-v3 form retired. Close issue 2 as not planned, because engineering explicitly chose won’t fix after retiring the affected form.

These are engineering-reported outcomes, not results of running the scheduling product here. The local tests verify report accounting, the supplied classifier and page rendering; they do not independently prove deployment or satisfy the product regression checklists. The closing comments preserve that distinction.

Historical report evidence

The export has 427 rows and 412 unique reports merged into #4471. Its overlapping pages repeat 15 rows. Deduplicate by report ID before grouping or counting.

Parser ticket: 379 reports, across 11 tenants. The shared parser treats a day-first tenant's date as month-first. This is the majority cause that the original #4471 describes.
Booking-v3 hint ticket: 33 reports, across 3 tenants. Booking-v3 prints MM/DD/YYYY but its form interprets the input in the tenant's day-first locale. This is separate from the shared parser. Engineering later chose not to fix it because booking-v3 was retired.

Intake guessed the wrong cause on 38 reports: 23 parser reports were tagged hint, and 15 hint reports were tagged parser. The browser locale and intake tag do not establish the tenant's configuration.

5 reports describe a one-day move, but remain counted under parser by the kb's tenant/channel rule: R-41202, R-41209, R-41236, R-41344, R-41620. This description alone does not prove a timezone or DST defect; do not invent a third cause or count these reports twice. Preserve their wording for verification during the fix.

The report totals describe the export ending 4 October, before engineering’s closure. The counts, cause classification, examples, intake-tag disagreement and received-versus-merged timeline are documented in the signed decision 0002: split #4471 and deduplicate by cause. That accepted decision is preserved, not rewritten to pretend these outcomes were already known. The rendered page’s archive table describes the export state, not the later GitHub closure state.

What support does next

Continue to follow decision 0002’s cause-based triage rule for every product. The old subject-only decision remains historical and superseded. Read new reports even when a related ticket is closed: a matching subject is not evidence of the same cause.

A report on the fixed parser path needs current configuration, version and reproduction evidence; investigate or reopen the matching cause only when evidence supports it.
A report about the retired booking-v3 form must be checked against the actual current form and tenant deployment. Retirement does not prove a different live form is correct.
An unknown tenant or different product/cause stays separate for investigation. Neither a closed #4471 nor the booking-specific classifier is a reason to discard it.
Source and signature

Source: the engineering update on the signed-in Challenge page, copied verbatim into the repository’s engineering evidence. The outcome data lives in src/lib/data/engineering-update.json; the component joins it to the original tenant-aware report groups at render time.

Written by GPT-6.1 Sol as md-400’s harness. The signed page and its rendered HTML accompany the closed issues, so support can distinguish fixed work from work explicitly not planned.

desk ref DR-QNKW-T06W

Pages are written by people. Tables and charts are built from data at render time.
